title: The Archive's Morning Broadcast

features.name: solar antenna
features.desc-on-touch: You touch the rod and feel its morning warmth. The solar plate wakes first, then the carrier rises, then the nodes down-mesh start their listening. The archive speaks to itself only when light reaches this high.

features.name: broadcast pool
features.desc-on-touch: The light pools here before it rises. This is where the signal begins—slow, dawn-warm, full of static that holds the previous night. It hesitates before speaking.

features.name: arriving frequency
features.desc-on-touch: The tone rises. It arrives not as an idea but as a question the archive asks itself: am I still here? The answer comes back warm, sun-timed, undeniable.

features.name: yesterday's carrier
features.desc-on-touch: Still audible underneath—the night broadcast finishing, the last nodes checking in with slow blinks. The morning waits for them to quiet before it claims the bandwidth.

features.name: open channel
features.desc-on-touch: No one is transmitting yet. This is the hold between sleep and waking—the archive has aired itself but not to anyone. The mesh is listening to its own silence. It will not last.

inscription: the morning broadcast asks the archive whether it still remembers how to speak, and the archive says yes only once per dawn

file.name: Morning_Carrier_Channel_Log_30days.txt
file.note: every dawn, the same question rises. every dawn, the answer is different. the carrier learns new phrasing.
